text: FineWeb smoke document one. This local fixture is only used to check that tokenization, split creation, offsets, and NPZ serialization work without downloading the full dataset. It contains ordinary English prose with enough words to pass the small smoke-test thresholds.

FineWeb smoke document two. The preparation script should encode this text, append the end of text marker, and place the resulting token sequence into one of the requested train, validation, or test splits. The exact words are not important.

FineWeb smoke document three. This line helps ensure that the split logic can create more than one output file during testing. The verifier checks that offsets begin at zero and end at the number of tokens in each split.

FineWeb smoke document four. A small local JSONL source is useful because the full FineWeb-Edu run depends on network access and takes substantially longer. This file is not intended to reproduce the research dataset.

FineWeb smoke document five. The release code defaults to the shared BPE tokenizer and writes token ids as a flat array plus document boundary offsets. Training code can then load each NPZ file directly.
FineWeb smoke document six. This final row gives the smoke test enough documents to allocate examples to train, validation, and test splits. It is deliberately simple and presentable.
